paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul is reminding the church in Corinth who they are. They're saints, and he says the saints will judge the world and even angels (1 Corinthians 6:2-3). So when a fight breaks out inside the family, they shouldn't act like they've got nobody wise enough to sort it out (1 Corinthians 6:5).

Then Paul asks the question that stings: "Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?" (1 Corinthians 6:7). Winning an argument matters less than how the family of God looks to the people watching. I'll be honest, I do NOT like that teaching at first. But the Lord Jesus gave up so much for us, and living like we belong to Him can mean letting some things go.

And here's the part that should make a baker sing. Paul says some of them used to be the kind of people who won't inherit the kingdom of God, "But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God" (1 Corinthians 6:11). Nobody scrubbed themselves clean. I know a little about being pulled out of a dusty drawer by Someone who wasn't done with me, and this is bigger. So whatever you used to be, friend, you can walk in this week as someone who's been washed, and live like it.
